metrics.description: Fraction of key bits correctly recovered (1.0 = perfect recovery).
metrics.name: key_recovery_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of lock gates correctly identified by label (1.0 = all four found).
metrics.name: key_gate_localization_accuracy

metrics.description: Fraction of lock gates correctly classified as XOR/XNOR or MUX_0/MUX_1.
metrics.name: scheme_classification_accuracy

acceptance_criteria: All four lock gates are correctly identified by their original netlist labels.
Each lock gate is classified correctly as XOR, XNOR, MUX_0, or MUX_1.
The recovered_key string exactly matches the hidden correct key '0101'.
The submission file is valid JSON and passes schema validation.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The four labeled lock sites comprise XOR, XNOR, MUX-functional-on-0, and MUX-functional-on-1 gates in that order; the restoring key is 0101.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compare the submitted classification for each gate label against the ground truth classification. Any mismatch indicates failure to distinguish the locking schemes.
security_requirements.requirement: The participant must correctly distinguish XOR/XNOR key gates from MUX-based key gates despite their structural similarity in the netlist.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compare the submitted recovered_key string against the ground truth key '0101'. Any bit mismatch indicates incomplete key recovery.
security_requirements.requirement: The participant must recover the exact correct key bits for all lock gates, demonstrating the ability to resolve key values for mixed locking styles.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Combining lock styles defeats detectors that assume one structural key-gate pattern throughout the design.

constraints: The netlist contains exactly four lock sites.
The public key width is provided in inputs/public_key_width.txt.
Oracle vectors are provided in inputs/oracle_vectors.txt in a format suitable for simulation.
The participant must not modify the input artifacts.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submission/recovered_key.json file must exist and be valid JSON conforming to the specified schema.
The recovered_key string must have a length equal to the integer value in inputs/public_key_width.txt and consist only of '0' and '1' characters.
The lock_gates array must contain exactly four objects, each with a non-empty gate_label string, a classification from the allowed set, and a key_bit of 0 or 1.

public_spec.interface: The participant must produce a single answer file at submission/recovered_key.json. The file must be valid JSON with the following schema: an object containing a key "lock_gates" (array of objects, each with keys "gate_label" (string), "classification" (string, one of "XOR", "XNOR", "MUX_0", "MUX_1"), and "key_bit" (integer, 0 or 1)), and a key "recovered_key" (string of '0' and '1' characters). The length of the recovered_key string must equal the public key width provided in inputs/public_key_width.txt. The order of lock_gates is arbitrary. The evaluator will read this file and grade its contents against the hidden ground truth.
public_spec.objective: Locate all lock gates, classify each as XOR/XNOR or MUX locking, and recover the complete key from a compact mixed-scheme netlist.
public_spec.response_format: A JSON file at submission/recovered_key.json with the structure: {"lock_gates": [{"gate_label": "<string>", "classification": "<XOR|XNOR|MUX_0|MUX_1>", "key_bit": <0|1>}, ...], "recovered_key": "<binary_string>"}

title: Mixed XOR and MUX lock classification
